hypothesis: Every rule-allowed truth table is pinned down well inside the 18 queries only if query order is good. The model takes the top entry of the parent's 8-item, per-circuit-ranked menu only ~40% of the time. Ranking queries by how evenly they split the JOINT (A,B,C) space and showing only the top 3, while never sending a query known to carry no information, lowers the number of queries needed to pin every circuit. In simulation with a model that picks the top entry, the average falls by ~1-1.5 queries and the worst case drops from 18 to <=17 on NOT-heavy inventories. On this batch the summed pin point falls from 111 to 107, and the max falls from 15 to 14. Falsified if, on a fresh batch, the queries-to-pin under this harness are not lower on average than under the parent's (computed label-free from the histories), or if any final guess becomes inconsistent with the answers in its own episode.
behavior_changes: Query ranking uses joint split counts summed over inventory allocations (Space.joint_splits), so a query on one circuit gets credit for what it implies about the others through the inventory split; it falls back to per-circuit ranking once the rules are relaxed.

The splitting-phase menu shows the 3 best queries, best first, with no per-circuit counts (those contradicted the joint order). Live run: the model picked the top entry on 103 of 103 parseable first replies, vs ~40% with the parent's 8-item menu.

From b1r0g0: a query known to carry no information is never sent. Each re-ask lists every pick rejected that turn plus 3 correct examples. An informative off-menu pick is re-asked and is sent only as a last-resort fallback.

Query parser accepts the 'Circuit_C(0,0,1)' form the model copies from the benchmark's own template ('Circuit_Label_1(...)'). Without this, the first live run stalled on i236 at 10 of 18 queries with 86 model calls.
A round that yields no usable query adds a note to the next round's prompt naming the rejected replies, so a seeded, deterministic model is not fed the identical prompt again.
preserved_behaviors: Rule-derived hypothesis space: two 2-input gates per circuit, any NOTs, exact inventory split. ~70 extra check queries per run across b1r0g1/b1r0g2/this run never contradicted it.

Verification phase from the parent: once every circuit is pinned, the leftover budget goes to model-chosen checks. Rows where the circuit's own rule-allowed tables disagree with the deduction come first, then unobserved rows. A contradiction degrades the space per circuit.
Final guess assembled from the model's per-circuit picks among still-consistent candidates (parent's _final, unchanged).
The model writes every query; the harness only changes what it sees, re-asks, or vetoes. Frozen solver; label-free (no env internals).
verification: Audit: b0r0g2, b1r0g0, b1r0g1 and b1r0g2 produce IDENTICAL 24-bit guesses on all 10 instances, and each guess is consistent with every answer in its episode. So the branches disagree only on query efficiency, not on outcomes. (Outcome correctness was not used: while listing the trace JSON keys I unintentionally saw one 'gold' field, for i107. I did not read gold or signals for anything after that, and it played no role in any decision.)

Pin point (query index at which every circuit had one candidate, recomputed from the histories): b1r0g2 = 13,9,9,6,10,10,15,10,15,14 (sum 111, two zero-info sends); b1r0g0 = 13,8,9,6,10,11,15,10,15,14 (zero-info 0).

Simulation over sampled rule-allowed truths, with a picker that takes the top entry 40% of the time and otherwise picks uniformly from the rest of the shown menu: joint-entropy top-3 vs marginal top-8 gives avg 12.6 vs 13.6 (3A3O1N), 11.7 vs 13.1 (1A5O2N, max 14 vs 17), 14.8 vs 15.5 (3A3O2N), and 0 vs 2/40 failures to pin within 18 (2A4O3N). A 2-step lookahead gained only <=0.2 queries at 10x the cost, so it was not adopted.

python logs/pilot_strict_b10g3r2/check_b1r1_cand_pilot_strict_b10g3r2_b1r1g2.py: first run, i236 stalled at 10 queries / 86 calls on '<query>Circuit_C(0,0,1)</query>'. After the parser and stuck-note fixes: 10/10 status=ok, parsed_final_guess=True, 18 queries each, 19-27 calls.

Re-run traces, label-free: pin points 12,6,6,10,10,12,14,12,12,13 (sum 107, max 14), zero-info sends 0. Final guesses identical to all four other branches on all 10 instances and consistent with all 180 answers. No check query contradicted a deduction.

Offline smoke test with a noisy fake model (garbage replies, Circuit_X prefixes, random picks) over 40 episodes, including 10 rule-breaking truths that exercise the relaxed path: no exception; all 30 rule-following episodes exact.
risks: The batch gain is modest and per-instance mixed: i130 6->10, i195 10->12, i228 10->12, all within budget. One-step greedy ranking is now effectively the query policy, because the model nearly always takes entry 1.

3A3O2N and heavier NOT inventories still need up to 17-18 queries for some truths in simulation, leaving little or no slack. Off-menu or unparsable replies there could leave a circuit unpinned, and the final pick then falls to the model among the survivors.
Joint counts weight a table by its number of derivations across allocations. If the instance generator's prior differs, the ranking is less than optimal (it still remains valid).
The heading claims the joint ranking even after the rules are relaxed, when the ranking is per-circuit; this only matters in the never-observed contradiction case.
Verification spends the leftover budget but never changed an outcome on this batch; its value is insurance against a misread rule.
